text.p: The sale of small Venezuelan aluminum company Alucasa set for Thursday has been postponed to give potential investors more time to assess the company, the government said on Tuesday.
The extended period will give bidders "more time to allow them to end the analyses they have been carrying out" state Deposits Guarantee Fund, FOGADE, said in release.
A base price of $45 million had been set for the company, which has a capacity of 20,000 tonnes per year.

Alucasa is 49 percent owned by state-owned aluminum company Alcasa and 51 percent owned by a consortium of 16 private investors and banks, some of which were taken over by FOGADE during the 1994-95 banking crisis.
